test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 09 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which single‑window telecom regulator’s April 2025 consultation on satellite‑based spectrum assignment complements India’s 6G backhaul ambitions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**TRAI**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI)** is the primary telecom regulator in India responsible for overseeing and managing policies related to telecommunications, broadcasting, and spectrum allocation.
 
• In April 2025, TRAI's consultation on satellite-based spectrum assignment is expected to align with India's **6G backhaul ambitions**, enabling high-speed and efficient data transmission for next-generation networks.
 
• Satellite-based spectrum assignment is crucial for expanding network connectivity to remote and rural areas, supporting the deployment of **6G technologies** that require ultra-reliable and low-latency communications.
 
• TRAI plays a pivotal role in ensuring a balanced and transparent allocation of spectrum resources while fostering innovation and competition in the telecom sector.
 
• The consultation process by TRAI aims to address the technical, economic, and regulatory challenges of spectrum allocation for satellite-based systems, facilitating India's long-term goals in advanced telecommunications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Internet Exchange of India (NIXI)**

 
 
• NIXI is a non-profit organization established to facilitate Internet exchange points in India, enabling efficient routing of domestic internet traffic.
 
• It primarily focuses on promoting the adoption of the **.IN domain** and ensuring a secure and robust internet infrastructure in India.
 
• While NIXI plays a vital role in internet governance, it does not regulate spectrum allocation or satellite-based systems.
 
 
 
• **Wireless Planning & Coordination (WPC)**
 
 
• The WPC Wing, under the Department of Telecommunications, is responsible for managing spectrum allocation and licensing for wireless communication services in India.
 
• WPC focuses on spectrum management for terrestrial and satellite-based communication, but its role is limited to execution and licensing rather than policy consultation.
 
 
 
• **National Informatics Centre (NIC)**
 
 
• NIC is a premier government organization under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), providing IT support and services to government bodies across India.
 
• While NIC is instrumental in developing e-governance applications and IT infrastructure, it is not involved in spectrum allocation or telecom regulation.
